ADO.NET

Write the rows of any IDataReader (a database query, DataTable.CreateDataReader(), ...) as a Parquet file, and read a Parquet file as a DbDataReader, which works with SqlBulkCopy, DataTable.Load and the like. This is in the ParquetNeo package.

using ParquetNeo.Data;

using var query = command.ExecuteReader();
using var output = File.Create("orders.parquet");
ParquetDataWriter.Write(query, output);

using var input = File.OpenRead("orders.parquet");
using var reader = new ParquetDataReader(input);
while (reader.Read())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{reader.GetInt64(0)} {reader.GetString(1)}");
}

The writer takes the type of each column from GetFieldType, and the nullability and the precision of decimals from the schema table of the reader. It writes row groups of a set size, so memory does not depend on the number of rows. WriteAsync is the asynchronous version.

ParquetDataReaderOptions chooses which columns to read, and takes a filter that skips row groups and pages that cannot hold the rows you want: see Skipping what is not needed.
